screen1-a1.where: The blue rounded square at the very top of the left column, with a white speech bubble in it.
screen1-a1.expectation: It takes me to my messages - the screen I am on now, which is titled 'Messages'.
screen1-a1.cue: The speech bubble picture, the fact that it is coloured blue while the other squares are grey, and the 'Messages' title next to it.

first_pass.why: A speech bubble is a real object that stands for a message, and the title of the screen matches it.

screen1-a2.where: The small magnifying glass in a square, top of the main area, left of 'Add Friends'.
screen1-a2.expectation: It opens a search. I assume a search of my messages because it sits under the 'Messages' title.

first_pass.why: A magnifying glass for search is a convention I know and there is nothing else it could reasonably mean here.

screen1-a3.where: The wide grey button at the top with a person-with-a-plus picture and the words 'Add Friends'.
screen1-a3.expectation: It opens a screen where I can add friends.

first_pass.why: The text says literally what it does.

screen1-a4.where: The small blue square with a white plus sign at the top right.
screen1-a4.expectation: It creates something new. I guess a new message, because this is the Messages screen, but it could be a new group or a new friend.
screen1-a4.cue: Only the plus sign. There is no word.

first_pass.why: A plus sign means 'add' or 'new' but not 'new what'. It is right next to 'Add Friends', which also adds something, so I cannot tell how the two differ.
first_pass.solution: Put a word next to the plus, for example 'New Message', so it is clear how it differs from 'Add Friends'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the blue plus shows what it adds, and whether that differs from 'Add Friends'
test_cases.action: Start on the Messages screen (the one headed 'Messages', with the speech-bubble square at the top left). Press the blue square with the white plus at the top right (not the 'Add Friends' button). Look at what opens and read its heading. (one try covering the same box on screen2-a4, screen14-a4)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the plus was for, or it is the same thing 'Add Friends' does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens has a heading in plain words that tells you what the plus did, and it is a different thing from 'Add Friends'
test_cases.what_happened: On the Messages screen I pressed the blue square with the white plus at the top right. After a moment a screen opened with the heading 'New Message', a 'To: Search your friends' field, and an 'Add Friends' button at the bottom. So it starts a new message. That is not the same as 'Add Friends', which is a separate button on that screen.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: The plus did what I first guessed, the heading says so in plain words, and it is different from 'Add Friends'. I would still like a word on the button, but my complaint does not hold.

screen1-a5.cue: The letters 'ATs' and the fact that they sit in a column under the messages button. Nothing else.

first_pass.solution: Show the full name of each item, and make the three distinguishable, for example with the full server name as visible text under each square.

It opened my whole profile page, with Edit Profile, Orbs Balance, Friends and so on. Later, on the profile page, I found that the status list (Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb, Invisible) opens from the picture and from the name there instead.

screen2-a11.cue: It is a round picture next to my account name, which is where apps usually put the user's picture.

first_pass.why: The picture is not me - it is a cartoon face. I only guess it is my profile because of where it is. It also overlaps the account strip next to it, so I cannot tell if it does something different from that strip.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'Your profile', or make the picture and the name one control that says so.

first_pass.why: Close is the conventional meaning, and it is where I expect it.

screen7-a2.expectation: Maybe it changes my picture, or opens a larger view of it, or changes the green 'online' dot. I do not know which.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing your big round picture does what you expected
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. On your page, press your big round picture near the top. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a2, screen19-a2, screen20-a2)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected from a picture
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: On my profile page I pressed my big round picture near the top. A panel slid up headed 'Change Online Status', with Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb, Invisible and 'Set a custom status'. I closed it with Back.

screen7-a2.closing_comment: Changing the status was one of the three things I guessed, and the panel heading says plainly what it is. But nothing about a picture of me says 'status', so I would not have picked it first.

screen7-a3.where: The white bubble to the right of my picture with a plus in a circle and the words 'What have you been reading?' in italics.
screen7-a3.expectation: I think it lets me write a short line of text that shows on my profile. I do not know if it has to be about reading.
screen7-a3.cue: The plus sign and the question.

first_pass.why: It is a question, not an instruction. I read it literally: it is asking about books I have read. I doubt that is really what it is for, but nothing tells me what it actually is.
first_pass.solution: Replace the question with a plain instruction, for example 'Add a status message'.

test_cases.targets: whether the speech bubble's purpose becomes plain once you press it
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press the speech bubble with the italic question beside your picture. Read the screen that opens, then leave it with the X without saving anything. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a3, screen19-a3, screen20-a3)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the screen that opens still does not tell you what it is for or who would see it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen that opens tells you in plain words what it is for
test_cases.what_happened: On my profile page the bubble next to my picture now said 'Today I learned...'. Earlier on this visit it had said 'What are you currently obsessed with?', and in the pictures it said three other things. I pressed it. A screen opened headed 'Set your status', with a preview of my profile card, a field labelled 'Status' and a 'Clear at: Tomorrow' row. I closed it with the X without saving.

screen7-a3.closing_comment: The screen it opens says in plain words that this is my status, and the preview shows it appears on my profile card. The bubble itself is still a question that changes every time I look, and it never says 'status'.

screen7-a4.where: My name 'Accessibility Testing' in large bold letters with a small down arrow.
screen7-a4.expectation: A list opens - maybe to switch accounts, maybe to change my name. I do not know which.
screen7-a4.cue: The small down arrow next to the name.

first_pass.why: The arrow tells me a list opens but not what is in it.
first_pass.solution: Add a word saying what the list is, for example 'Switch account'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing your name with the small arrow opens what you expected
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press your name with the small down arrow under your picture. Look at what opens. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a4, screen19-a4, screen20-a4)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected from your name and the arrow
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: On my profile page I pressed my name with the small down arrow. The same 'Change Online Status' panel opened as from the picture. I closed it.

screen7-a4.closing_comment: I expected switching accounts or changing my name. It changes my online status, which has nothing to do with my name. The panel is clearly labelled, but the name did not tell me.

screen7-a5.where: The wide blue button with a pencil and 'Edit Profile'.
screen7-a5.expectation: It opens a screen where I can edit my profile.
screen7-a5.cue: The words 'Edit Profile' and the pencil.

first_pass.why: Literal text.

screen7-a6.where: The left one of two tabs under the Edit Profile button, 'Main', in blue with a blue line under it.
screen7-a6.expectation: It shows the main part of my profile - what I am looking at now.
screen7-a6.cue: The word 'Main', its blue colour and underline which say it is the current tab.

first_pass.why: 'Main' is not very descriptive, but it is clearly the selected tab and the content under it is what it shows.

screen7-a7.expectation: It shows a list of things I want - I assume things from the shop, but it does not say.

first_pass.why: A wishlist of what? This is a chat app. I can guess it relates to the Shop further down, but that is a guess.
first_pass.solution: Say what the list holds, for example 'Shop wishlist'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing 'Wishlist' tells you what the list is
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press 'Wishlist' and read what appears. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a7, screen19-a7, screen20-a7)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the list is or what goes in it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears explains in plain words what the list is
test_cases.what_happened: On my profile page I pressed 'Wishlist'. The tab showed 'No hearts yet', then 'Browse the Shop and heart the items you love to add them here', and an 'Add Item' button.

screen7-a7.closing_comment: It says plainly that it is a list of Shop items, which is what I guessed. 'Heart the items' is a little figurative, but the meaning is clear.

screen7-a8.where: The small X at the top right inside the purple-bordered card 'Amp up your profile'.
screen7-a8.expectation: It closes or removes that card.
screen7-a8.cue: The X in the corner of the card.

first_pass.why: An X in the corner of a card to dismiss it is clear.

screen7-a9.where: The left button in the card, with a round swirl symbol and 'Get Nitro'.
screen7-a9.expectation: I think it takes me to buy something called Nitro. I do not know what Nitro is.

first_pass.why: 'Nitro' is a word that means something chemical, or a speed boost. In this app it is a name for something I have not been told about. The card heading 'Amp up your profile' is also a figure of speech. So I know I would 'get' something, but not what.
first_pass.solution: Say what Nitro is on the button or right under it, for example 'Nitro - paid subscription'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing 'Get Nitro' tells you what Nitro is and whether it costs money
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. In the box 'Amp up your profile', press 'Get Nitro'. Read the page, then go back without buying anything. (If that box is not there, tell me and use 'Nitro' in the bottom bar instead.) (one try covering the same box on screen8-a9, screen19-a9, screen20-a9)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you still cannot tell what Nitro is, or you only find out it costs money once you are there
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the page tells you plainly what Nitro is and what it costs, and that matches what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: The 'Amp up your profile' card with 'Get Nitro' was not on my profile page in the live app, so as you said I used 'Nitro' in the bottom bar instead. A page opened headed 'Discord NITRO - Unleash more fun on Discord', with two plans: Nitro at $9.99 a month and Nitro Basic at $2.99 a month, each with a list of features and a 'Get' button. I went back without buying anything. A red strip at the top also asked me to verify my email.

screen7-a9.closing_comment: Now I know Nitro is a paid subscription and what it costs. But I only found out that it costs money once I was on that page - the button never said so.

screen7-a10.where: The right button in the card, with a shop-front picture and 'Shop'.
screen7-a10.cue: The word 'Shop' and the shop-front picture.

first_pass.why: It says Shop. I do not know what they sell, but I know where the button goes.

screen7-a11.where: A wide grey row 'Orbs Balance' with three faint dots on the right.
screen7-a11.expectation: It shows how many 'Orbs' I have, whatever those are. Maybe it opens more detail about them.
screen7-a11.cue: The word 'Balance', which suggests an amount of something.

first_pass.why: I do not know what Orbs are. Literally, an orb is a sphere. 'Balance' tells me it is a count, but a count of what, and why I would press it, I cannot tell.
first_pass.solution: One line explaining what Orbs are, for example 'Orbs: points you earn by ...'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing 'Orbs Balance' tells you what orbs are
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press 'Orbs Balance'. Read what opens, then close it. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a11, screen19-a11, screen20-a11)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you still cannot tell what orbs are, or what opens is not what you expected
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens explains orbs in plain words and matches what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: On my profile page I pressed 'Orbs Balance'. A panel slid up with a question-mark icon, an orb symbol with '0', and two buttons: 'Redeem Orbs in Shop' and 'Earn Orbs'. I closed it with Back.

screen7-a11.closing_comment: From the buttons I can work out that orbs are points you earn and spend in the Shop, which is roughly what I guessed. Nothing on the panel says in a sentence what an orb is.

screen7-a12.where: The wide grey row 'Friends' with an arrow pointing right.
screen7-a12.expectation: It opens my list of friends.

first_pass.why: Literal text; the arrow says it goes to another screen.

first_pass.why: The text is literal and even says who can see it. I am a little puzzled why I would write a note on my own profile, but what it does is clear.

screen7-a14.where: The first item in the floating bar at the bottom: a crest-like picture with a red dot, labelled 'Quests'.
screen7-a14.expectation: It opens something called Quests. I do not know what quests are in a chat app - maybe tasks to earn rewards.
screen7-a14.cue: The word 'Quests' and the red dot, which means something new is there.

first_pass.why: A quest is a journey or a mission in a game. The word is a metaphor here and I do not know what I would actually be doing.
first_pass.solution: Say what it is literally, for example 'Tasks for rewards'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing 'Quests' tells you what quests are
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the round picture at the bottom left, next to your name. Press 'Quests' in the bar at the bottom. Read what opens, then close it. (one try covering the same box on screen8-a14, screen19-a14, screen20-a14)

screen7-a15.expectation: It opens the shop - the same as the 'Shop' button in the card above, I assume.

first_pass.why: It says Shop.

first_pass.why: A speech bubble stands for messages. It is in the same place as on the Messages screen, where it was blue and the title said 'Messages'. Grey now means I am somewhere else.

screen32-a2.where: The large title at the top, 'Accessibility Testin's server', with a small arrow pointing right.
screen32-a2.expectation: It opens information or settings about this server. I do not know which.
screen32-a2.cue: The small right arrow after the title, which means it goes somewhere.

first_pass.why: It looks like a heading, and headings usually do nothing. The arrow says it is pressable, but not what it opens. The name is also cut off or misspelled - 'Testin's'.
first_pass.solution: Put a small text such as 'Server settings' or 'Server info' under the title, or a separate labelled button.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the heading with the small arrow opens what you expected
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the first 'ATs' square in the left column. Press the heading at the top of that screen (the name with a small arrow). Look at what opens, then close it. (one try covering the same box on screen26-a2, screen27-a2, screen28-a2, screen29-a2, screen30-a2, screen31-a2, screen33-a2, screen34-a2, screen35-a2)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected from a heading
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the first 'ATs' square, then the heading 'Accessibility Testin's server' with the small arrow. A panel slid up with the server name, '1 Online, 1 Member', four labelled buttons (Boost, Invite, Notifications, Settings), 'Mark As Read', 'Resume your server setup', 'Create Channel', 'Create Category', 'Create Event', and more settings below. I closed it with Back.

screen32-a2.closing_comment: It opened information and settings about the server, which is what I guessed, and everything in it has a text label.

screen32-a3.where: The wide grey 'Search' button with a magnifying glass under the title.
screen32-a3.expectation: It opens a search, I assume within this server.

first_pass.why: Literal.

screen32-a4.where: The small square to the right of Search with a person and a plus sign.
screen32-a4.expectation: It invites people to this server, or it adds a friend. I cannot tell which.

first_pass.why: On the Messages screen the same kind of person-with-plus picture had the words 'Add Friends' next to it. Here there are no words, and on a server screen it could mean 'invite to server' instead.
first_pass.solution: Put a word under it, e.g. 'Invite'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the person-with-plus picture settles whether it adds a friend or invites someone here
test_cases.action: From the Messages screen, press the first 'ATs' square in the left column. Press the picture of a person with a plus at the top right. Read what opens, then close it. test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens settles it plainly
test_cases.what_happened: On the server screen I pressed the person-with-a-plus picture at the top right. A panel slid up headed 'Invite a friend', with a search field saying 'Invite friends to Accessibility Testin's server', a row of share tiles, and 'No friends to invite yet'. I closed it.

screen32-a4.closing_comment: The panel settles it: it invites people to this server. But the same picture on the Messages screen goes to 'Add Friends', which is a different screen, so I still cannot tell which one it is before pressing.

screen32-a5.where: The small square at the top right with a calendar picture.
screen32-a5.expectation: It shows events for this server, or lets me schedule one. I am guessing.

first_pass.why: A calendar is a real object, but it could mean view events, create an event, or a date setting. No text.
first_pass.solution: A text label such as 'Events'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the calendar picture settles what it does

test_cases.what_happened: On the server screen I pressed the calendar picture. A panel slid up headed 'Events' with a 'Create' link and 'There are no upcoming events. Schedule an event for any planned activity in your server.' I closed it.

screen32-a5.closing_comment: It is the server's events, with the option to create one - exactly my first guess - and the heading says so.

screen32-a6.where: The first 'ATs' square in the left column, which is blue on this screen while the other two are grey.
screen32-a6.expectation: It opens this server - the one I am on now.
screen32-a6.cue: It is blue like the selected item, and the title says 'Accessibility Testin's server', and 'ATs' could be the initials of that.

first_pass.why: Because it is highlighted and the title names the server, I can connect them. It is a deduction, but a reliable one.

screen32-a7.where: A row with a hexagon-shield picture and 'Server Boosts' in light grey.
screen32-a7.expectation: It opens something about 'boosts' for the server - maybe paying to improve it. I do not know what a boost is.

first_pass.why: 'Boost' is figurative. Boost what, and how? The row does not say whether it is information or a purchase.
first_pass.solution: Say what it literally is, for example 'Pay to add server features'.

test_cases.what_happened: On the server screen I pressed 'Server Boosts'. A page opened headed 'Server Boosts', with counts (0 Available, 0 Spent, 0 Total), 'Levels' (your server will 'level up' with enough Boosts), cards listing perks per level, 'Additional Perks', and a 'Boost This Server' button fixed at the bottom. I scrolled down once and saw no price anywhere. The badge picture in the perks area also changed from 'STAR' to 'GOAT' while I watched. I closed it with the X without buying anything.

screen32-a7.closing_comment: I still do not know what a boost literally is or whether it costs money. The page is full of what boosts unlock, but never says what one is or how you get one.
